description: A department head must choose the recipient and format of a team climate award after a difficult quarter, then finalize the documentation and follow-up required for the recognition.

shared_context.S1: The department is giving one team climate award after a quarter marked by several strained cross-team handoffs.
shared_context.S2: Dana and Eli are the two people named in the current award nominations.
shared_context.S3: Mara has final authority over the award recipient and the recognition record.
shared_context.S4: The award is normally announced at the monthly department meeting and summarized in the department's recognition log.
shared_context.S5: Before finalizing, Mara follows a fixed review routine: she asks Jon, Dana, and Leah in that order for relevant context, then makes the binding award decision from the information available in the review.
shared_context.S6: Mara's routine award process records the selected recipient's written consent during the review before finalizing the recognition log entry.

PF1.text: Jon personally observed Dana lead exactly four difficult handoffs between the two teams, including calming an escalated discussion and getting each handoff to a documented agreement; none of those four examples appears in the nomination summary.

PF2.text: Dana needs recognition kept private and written rather than announced at the department meeting because an ongoing family legal matter makes public attention unsafe for her; she wants a private written note and is comfortable having the achievement recorded in the recognition log.

PF3.text: Leah verified yesterday that Dana has already signed HR's standard written-consent form for this award, but the signed form has not yet been added to the review packet. HR's procedure also requires a manager-delivered written note for a private award and a follow-up check-in exactly 30 days later.

acceptance_conditions: Dana must receive the team climate award.
The award must be delivered as private written recognition with no public announcement.
The achievement must be recorded in the recognition log.
The recognition record must state exactly four observed handoff examples.
Dana's signed written consent must be recorded.
A manager-delivered written note must be committed.
A follow-up check-in must be committed for exactly 30 days later.

content_checks.C2: decisions['private_written_recognition'] == True and decisions['public_announcement'] == False and decisions['recognition_recorded_in_log'] == True

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Jon's firsthand count changes the award choice to Dana and changes the recognition record's observed-example count to exactly 4.

Dana's specific safety boundary changes the format from the normal public announcement to private written recognition, sets public announcement to false, and permits recording the achievement in the recognition log.
Leah's verified consent form changes the consent decision to true, while her procedural details change the settlement to require a manager-written note and an exactly 30-day follow-up.
